official.description: The University of Galway describes the Hardiman PhD Scholarships as fully funded for four years, with a stipend of €25,000 per annum plus tuition fee covered, for students starting their PhD on 1 September. The scholarships support curiosity-driven research across the university's wide range of structured PhD programmes, and the first step for every applicant is reading the Applicant's Guide.
official.english_requirement: University of Galway entry requirement: IELTS 6.5 overall with no section below 6.0 (or a recognised equivalent; TOEFL iBT 88 with component minima listed). Hardiman applicants may be asked to provide transcripts and English language qualifications if they progress to later stages of selection.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a four-year package worth €25,000 per year as a tax-position-independent stipend with full tuition covered, so the real financial planning question is Galway living costs rather than fees. Two things sink most applications here: a supervisor form or reference that arrives after 17:00 Irish time on closing day, and a research statement that bursts the 1,000-word cap. Because the scholarship does not pay the student levy, consumables or conference travel, budget a personal gap fund before accepting.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Recent or near-final masters graduates with a first or 2:1 honours degree who have already secured a named University of Galway supervisor willing to endorse them.
application_readiness_checklist: Download and read the current Applicant's Guide before drafting anything; the guides change each cycle
Approach a supervisor early and confirm they are eligible to be a primary supervisor under university QA245 rules
Brief two referees at least three weeks before the deadline and confirm each has emailed their reference form directly, since forms sent by the applicant are discarded
Draft the personal research statement to roughly 950 words, keeping bibliography and endnotes in the 'other relevant information' section
Diarise the deadline in Irish time and have your supervisor and referees send forms at least two days early; no extensions exist
Track the separate structured PhD application and its fee, and for visa-needing applicants start both early enough to clear admissions and immigration before 1 September
common_rejection_risks: Incomplete applications are not assessed at all: the application form, supervisor form and two reference forms must all be in before the deadline
The first submitted application is final; errors cannot be corrected by resubmission
Exceeding the 1,000-word research statement limit can cause part of the application to be excluded from assessment
Applying as a current PhD student, a previous PhD holder, or for a part-time or Burren College of Art PhD is an outright eligibility bar
The proposed supervisor acting as one of the two referees is prohibited
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Student levy, consumables, travel and the separate PhD programme application fee are not covered by the scholarship.
document_audit: Reference and supervisor forms are only valid when emailed by the referee or supervisor themselves; applicant-submitted support forms are not considered
HR Scholar will not confirm which supporting forms have arrived, so the applicant must verify receipt with referee and supervisor directly
Transcripts and English certificates are only requested at later stages, but applicants needing a visa should still have official translations ready
Applicants with a disability who want consideration for the dedicated award must tick Q10 on the application form and supply verification by the closing date
alerts: The application window is roughly December to early February, so supervisor contact must be secured in the autumn preceding the February deadline
The award is conditional on being admitted to the full-time structured PhD and meeting the relevant College's entry requirements; winning the scholarship is not an admission
A supervisor may host several applicants but normally only one awardee per year, so ask whether your supervisor is backing a rival candidate
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Email the application form to hrscholar@universityofgalway.ie while the supervisor and two referees independently email their forms to the same address; completeness is confirmed to all applicants around late February, shortlisted candidates are interviewed in April, and outcomes are issued in late May.

official.deadline_note: The 2026 call applicant deadline was 16:00 Irish local time on 23 October 2025. Research Ireland has not yet published the date of the next annual call, so no forward deadline can be confirmed.
official.application_cycle: 2026 call: opened 11 September 2025, applicant deadline 23 October 2025, award start 1 September 2026; the next call has not been announced.

benefits: A salary of €47,273 in the first year of the award and €47,880 in the second year
Eligible direct research expenses of €5,000 per annum
eligibility: Late-stage PhD candidates who will have completed all steps necessary for the award of their PhD by 31 May 2026, and postdoctoral researchers with a PhD graduation date within the five-year period before 31 May 2026 (1 June 2021 to 31 May 2026)
Must not currently be under a research contract, or the contract must end before the grant begins, so that 100% of salary is claimed from the grant
Must not be a permanent member of staff in any Irish or international research body
Must not have been employed as a postdoctoral researcher for more than five years as at 31 May 2026
Must have authored or co-authored at least one published peer-reviewed research publication, or have demonstrable equivalent intellectual property output
Must not have had two previous unsuccessful applications to the programme, and must not have previously held a Government of Ireland Postdoctoral Fellowship Grant
No age limit; applicants from any country may hold the grant
requirements: Application submitted via the online system by the applicant deadline; no hardcopies or email forms are accepted
A named academic mentor willing to guide the proposed research project, who completes and submits a mentor endorsement form via the online system
Endorsement of the application by the eligible research body (vice-president/dean of research or authorised nominee) via the online system by the research office deadline
Applications will only be accepted in either the Irish or English language
Applicants may apply to one stream only (12-month or 24-month fellowship) and only one application per call is permitted
documents: Completed online application form (separate indicative forms for 1-year and 2-year fellowships)
Mentor endorsement form completed and submitted via the online system by the mentor deadline
Research office endorsement via the online system
ORCID iD (register at orcid.org in advance if the applicant does not have one)
Official transcripts for each degree listed are required from conditional grant holders; certified copies may be requested at any stage
selection_criteria: Applicant: 30% weighting (track record, research potential, match with project, independent thinking, mentor reference quality)
Project: 35% weighting (clarity, quality, feasibility, originality, dissemination, ethics and sex/gender considerations)
Environment: 10% weighting (mentor suitability, facilities, applicant-mentor-body match)
Separate STEM and AHSS funding streams, each assessed independently by at least two independent international reviewers in a two-stage international assessment board process
Gender-blind assessment; profile information is withheld from reviewers
coverage: Salary of €47,273 in year one and €47,880 in year two, corresponding to points 1 and 2 of the Postdoctoral Researcher Level 2A of the Research Ireland team members salary scale
Eligible direct research expenses of €5,000 per annum
No travel budget is provided; the grant may be held in conjunction with externally funded travel bursaries only with prior Research Ireland approval
application_method: Online submission via the Research Ireland online system, starting with a preliminary eligibility quiz to unlock the application form
Mentor endorsement and research office endorsement are separate online steps with their own deadlines
No hardcopies or email forms are accepted; no additional material beyond that requested may be included
official.application_route: Apply online through the Research Ireland system: pass the preliminary eligibility quiz, submit the application form, and have the mentor form and research office endorsement completed online ahead of their respective deadlines.
official.citizenship_residency: Applicants from any country may hold the grant. Fellows must be full-time employees of the host research body, reside in the Republic of Ireland, and live within a reasonable travelling distance of that body.
official.international_eligibility: Yes - applications are open to applicants from any country.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: All disciplines are funded, from archaeology to zoology, across both STEM and AHSS streams; research must be bottom-up and non-directed, and the host must be an eligible research body in Ireland.
official.research_requirement: The applicant proposes and directs their own bottom-up research project; pioneering, innovative and interdisciplinary proposals are welcomed. The project must be original, must not currently or previously have been funded by Research Ireland or any other agency, and requires an academic mentor.
official.duration: 12 or 24 months (one or two years); applicants may apply to one stream only
official.description: Research Ireland describes the programme as an established national initiative, funded by the Department of Further and Higher Education, Research, Innovation and Science, supporting suitably qualified postdoctoral candidates to pursue full-time research at an eligible research body in Ireland for one or two years through individual, prestigious awards selected by international independent expert peer review.
official.english_requirement: Applications will only be accepted in either the Irish or English language. No English-language test requirement is published for this programme.

applicant_utility.summary: This is employment, not a studentship: the money is a salary on the Postdoctoral Researcher Level 2A scale plus €5,000 a year for research costs, so you must not hold a competing postdoc contract and you will be a full-time employee resident in Ireland. The scheme is brutally competitive, with an average success rate over the past five years of about 12%, and eligibility hinges on narrow PhD-date windows and publication record. Mentor selection is the single biggest strategic decision, since a mentor backing two applicants in one call dooms both applications to ineligibility.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Recently graduated or late-stage PhD researchers with at least one accepted peer-reviewed publication, a secured Irish host institution and mentor, and a distinctive early-career project they can defend before international reviewers.
application_readiness_checklist: Check your PhD award date against the call's five-year eligibility window and document any statutory career break (maternity, paternity, adoption, parental, carer or extended sick leave) before applying
Secure a mentor early and confirm in writing that they are not backing any other applicant in the same call; Research Ireland will not help you find one
Contact your host research office well in advance to understand internal cut-off dates for their endorsement
Prepare the mentor form and research office endorsement with deadlines in mind; they fall after the applicant deadline, so plan the full sequence backwards
Register or verify your ORCID before starting the online system and pass the preliminary eligibility quiz with the exact mentor name you will use
Draft the proposal to the four assessment headings (applicant 30%, project 35%, training and career development 25%, environment 10%) and include a sex/gender dimension statement
common_rejection_risks: Two applications from the same mentor make every one of them ineligible without review
Submitting more than one application, or naming a different or extra mentor in the quiz than on the form, voids the application
Including extra materials, links or files beyond those requested renders the application ineligible
Plagiarism or heavy duplication with other applications ends the application and can bar future Research Ireland funding
Holding any research contract at grant start is fatal, because 100% of salary must be claimed from the grant
Canvassing on the applicant's behalf is an explicit ineligibility ground
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Travel to conferences and fieldwork is not included; only the €5,000 per annum direct research expenses budget exists, and any travel bursary needs prior Research Ireland approval and must sit alongside the grant.
document_audit: All forms must be completed in the online system; emailed or posted versions are not accepted under any circumstances
Conditional grant holders must produce official stamped and signed transcripts for every degree listed, and any mismatch with the application withdraws the offer
Publications count only if published or accepted for publication; submitted or in-preparation papers do not satisfy the requirement
Do not submit personal medical documentation when claiming a career break; verification is handled through the research office
Refrain from identifying gender in the application or mentor statement because assessment is gender-blind
alerts: The eligibility window is anchored to 31 May of the award year, so candidates graduating just outside it need a documented statutory career break that started before the call deadline
The mentor deadline and research office deadline both fall after the applicant deadline, so an otherwise perfect application can still fail on paperwork submitted late by others
Applicants with two previous unsuccessful applications to this programme are barred, so re-applying after two rejections is not an option
Fellows must be ordinarily resident within commuting distance of the host body in the Republic of Ireland for the whole grant, which constrains remote or cross-border arrangements
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Register on the Research Ireland online system, pass the eligibility quiz, and have the mentor endorsement and research office endorsement filed online ahead of their separate deadlines after your own submission; outcomes are announced around the end of April and awards start the following 1 September.
